neighbours.label: taking on another's identity, role or customs (try on, adoption of, take on her identity, adopted into)
fire: In pretend play, children try on the roles of parents, doctors and shopkeepers.
The swindler planned to take on his dead cousin's identity and collect the pension.
The court's outward adoption of Persian dress was mocked by the old nobles.
Rice farming was adopted into the island's culture only two centuries ago.
For the film she assumed the persona of a retired jazz singer.
Immigrant families often take up the customs of their new neighbours within a generation.
The actor slipped into the role of the villain without any rehearsal.
Teenagers sometimes borrow the manners and slang of their favourite celebrities.
quiet: In pretend play, children often argue about who gets the biggest toy.
The swindler planned to leave the country before the pension office noticed.
The court's taste for Persian dress was mocked by the old nobles.
Rice farming has been part of the island's economy for two centuries.
For the film she recorded several songs with a retired jazz singer.
Immigrant families often live close to their new neighbours within a generation.
The actor met the director of the villain's scenes without any rehearsal.
Teenagers sometimes follow the news about their favourite celebrities.

notes: card: top examples are 'try on' the lives of others, 'adoption of' customs, 'take on her identity', 'adopted into' a culture, 'exist in' states. Near misses keep the topics but drop the taking-on.
